fix: Return a distinct :deferred word from fn-own-bp-transit-submit-result and fn-owner-transit-decide for :defer decisions, and :duplicate for :have. Class :clock-unusable as :deferred in fn-olog-bp-app-class. Have fn-tcl-delivery-refuse-reason map deferral to No Resources (or Retransmit), and keep :deferred apart from :refused in fnn-bpapp-deliver's tally.

reviewer: books/owner.lisp:1674: fn-own-bp-transit-submit-result maps every non-:want decision to :refused. That includes fn-peer-decide-transfer's :defer :staged/:busy/:fenced/:disk-slow/:inflight-limit/:capacity (books/peer-inbound.lisp:517-536, 619-622). Only the owner-queue check yields :busy. The host's second gate at host/native/owner.lisp:3859-3863 also returns :refused for any kind other than :want. Clock failure at host/native/bp-app.lisp:129-132 returns :clock-unusable, which fn-olog-bp-app-class (books/owner-log.lisp:561) classes as :refused. bp-app.lisp:262 then returns (list :refused app-result) with app-result = :refused or :clock-unusable. fn-tcl-delivery-refuse-reason (books/tcpcl-delivery.lisp:45-49) gives No Resources only for :busy/:capacity/:persistence, so these transient cases go out as XFER_REFUSE Not Acceptable. The transient/permanent distinction is lost at the boundary, against the AGENTS.md rule. Severity is medium: fenced and clock-unusable are rare, but stage-busy deferrals under load are plausible.
scenario: A BP delivery of a wanted article arrives while the owner is fenced (recovery pending), while the node stage is non-empty, or at a moment the wall clock is unusable (the TCPCL tally's wall error). The NNTP path answers these with 436/431 (retry). The BP path returns :refused, logged as `refused`, and the delivery plan sends XFER_REFUSE with reason Not Acceptable for an already-acknowledged custody. An RFC 9174 sender treats that as final and drops the bundle, so the article is lost although nothing about it was unacceptable. AGENTS.md: 'Uncertain, refused and accepted stay distinct at every boundary'.
title: BP-carried transit collapses transient deferrals and an unusable clock into a permanent refusal (TCPCL XFER_REFUSE Not Acceptable)
